items.title: Section: Two Underlying Meanings — Purified Aspiration in the First Three, Purified Conduct in the Remaining Seven

items.zh: 云何復名如是略義？謂此十法略顯二義。一者、顯示意樂清淨；二者、顯示加行清淨。當知前三，顯示菩薩意樂清淨；其餘七種，顯示菩薩加行清淨。
items.en:
Second, the brief meaning; first, posing the question. What, then, is meant by this brief summary?
Second, naming it. These ten dharmas, in brief, display two meanings.
Third, listing them. First, displaying purified aspiration. Second, displaying purified conduct.
Fourth, mapping them. One should understand that the first three display the bodhisattva's own purified aspiration; the remaining seven display the bodhisattva's own purified conduct.

items.title: Section: The Full Sequence Narrated — Why Faith Must Come First and Offering to the Tathāgata Last

items.zh: 如是十法次第云何？謂諸菩薩，於大菩提先深淨信。次於有苦諸有情類，發起悲愍。起悲愍時，如是誓願：我應拔濟一切有情，令其安樂，而起慈心。起慈心已，一切能捨，於身命財無所顧戀。無顧戀已，即為彼義精勤加行，無有厭倦。無厭倦已，善知諸論。善知論已，如世間轉即如是知。知世間已，若自煩惱率爾現行，深生慚愧。生慚愧已，不隨煩惱自在而行，便能獲得堅力持性。由正獲得堅力持性，於正加行能無退轉，無量善法運運增長，能於如來奉獻上妙正行供養、財敬供養，是故最後供養如來。是名十法次第修證。
items.en:
Third, the sequence; first, posing the question. What is the sequence of these ten dharmas?
Second, explaining. Bodhisattvas, first, towards great awakening, hold a deep, pure faith. Next, towards suffering sentient beings, compassionate concern arises. Having given rise to compassionate concern, this very vow follows: I should rescue and deliver every sentient being, bringing them to ease — and loving-kindness arises. Having given rise to loving-kindness, one is able to relinquish everything, harbouring no attachment to body, life, or wealth. Having become free of attachment, one diligently applies effort for that very aim, without weariness. Having become free of weariness, one masters treatises. Having mastered treatises, one comes to know the world's own way of turning, exactly as it is. Having known the world, should one's own affliction suddenly manifest, deep conscientiousness arises. Having given rise to conscientiousness, one no longer follows affliction's own sway, and is thereby able to attain firm resolve. Precisely by genuinely attaining firm resolve, correct applied effort suffers no regression, immeasurable wholesome dharmas continuously increasing — one is thereby able to offer the Tathāgata excellent conduct as offering, and material offerings of wealth and reverence; this is why offering to the Tathāgata comes last.
Third, the conclusion. This is called the sequence in which these ten dharmas are cultivated and realised.

items.title: Section: These Ten Dharmas Purify Every Ground Alike — Closing the Chapter on the Grounds, and Opening the Chapter on Conduct With Four Kinds Named

items.zh: 當知如是十種善法，於一切地能淨修治。菩薩始從勝解行地，乃至最後到究竟地，於此一切菩薩地中，當知略有四菩薩行。何等為四？一者、波羅蜜多行，二者、菩提分法行，三者、神通行，四者、成熟有情行。
items.en:
Third, the total conclusion. One should understand that these ten wholesome dharmas are able to purify every one of the grounds alike.
Within the Basic Section, the Bodhisattva Stage, the third yoga foundation of ultimate practice, the chapter on conduct, part four.
Eighth chapter, conduct; first, briefly listing the four kinds of conduct; first, naming them. A bodhisattva, beginning from the ground of resolute practice all the way through to the final ground of ultimate accomplishment, across all these bodhisattva grounds, should be understood to have, in brief, four kinds of bodhisattva conduct.
Second, posing the question. What are the four?
Third, listing them. First, the conduct of the perfections. Second, the conduct of the factors of awakening. Third, the conduct of spiritual powers. Fourth, the conduct of maturing sentient beings.

items.title: Section: Ten Perfections Named — Six Already Known, and Four Reaching Only to the Seventh Ground and Beyond

items.zh: 前說六種波羅蜜多，及方便善巧波羅蜜多、願波羅蜜多、力波羅蜜多、智波羅蜜多，如是十種波羅蜜多，總名波羅蜜多行。
items.en: Fourth, explaining; first, distinguishing the four kinds individually; first, distinguishing; first, the conduct of the perfections; first, naming the ten. The six perfections already explained, together with the perfection of skilful means, the perfection of vow, the perfection of power, and the perfection of knowledge — these ten perfections together are called the conduct of the perfections.

items.title: Section: Skilful Means in Twelve Aspects — Six Turned Inward Towards One's Own Practice, Six Turned Outward Towards Maturing Beings

items.zh: 如前所說十二行相方便善巧，當知說名方便善巧波羅蜜多。
items.en:
Second, explaining the final four; first, the primary meaning; first, skilful means. The twelve aspects of skilful means already explained should be understood as named the perfection of skilful means.
Commentary: Regarding "the twelve aspects of skilful means already explained" — one should understand this exactly as explained in the earlier chapter on the factors of awakening.

items.title: Section: Five Great Vows, and the Ten Vows Springing From Them — Amitābha's Forty-Eight, Kṣitigarbha's Hell-Vow

items.zh: 如前所說五種大願，當知名願波羅蜜多。
items.en:
Second, vow. The five great vows already explained should be understood as named the perfection of vow.
Commentary: Regarding "the five great vows already explained" — one should understand this exactly as explained in the earlier chapter on the factors of awakening.

items.title: Section: The Ten Powers in Full — From Knowing What Is and Is Not Possible to the Power of Exhausted Contamination

items.zh: 所有十力加行清淨，當知名力波羅蜜多。
items.en:
Third, power. Purified applied effort regarding all ten powers should be understood as named the perfection of power.
Commentary: Regarding "purified applied effort regarding all ten powers" — the chapter on the lineage possessing power says: a bodhisattva, having genuinely known the correct causal relationship displayed by this inner wisdom, diligently cultivates, causing the lineage-nature of the power of knowing what is and is not possible to gradually grow pure, gradually grow strong. It further says: a bodhisattva, having genuinely known that karma once performed is never lost and karma never performed never bears fruit, diligently cultivates, causing the lineage-nature of the power of knowing one's own karma to gradually grow pure, gradually grow strong. It further says: a bodhisattva, whether receiving correct instruction from another, or giving undistorted instruction to others, is able to cause the remaining eight powers' own lineage-nature to gradually grow pure, gradually grow strong.

items.title: Section: Subsequently-Attained Wisdom Distinguished From Root Wisdom — The Perfection That Completes All Ten

items.zh: 於一切法如實安立清淨妙智，當知名智波羅蜜多。今於此中，能取勝義無分別轉清淨妙慧，當知名慧波羅蜜多。能取世俗有分別轉清淨妙智，當知名智波羅蜜多。如是名為二種差別。
items.en:
Fourth, knowledge; first, explaining its own nature. Knowledge that genuinely, correctly establishes every dharma exactly as it is, itself wondrous and pure, should be understood as named the perfection of knowledge.
Commentary: Regarding "knowledge that genuinely, correctly establishes every dharma" — the chapter on the qualities of a bodhisattva says: bodhisattvas possess, in brief, four kinds of establishment; only the Tathāgatas and bodhisattvas are able to correctly posit and correctly establish these, not any other being whatsoever — not a god, not a human, not a renunciate, not a brahmin — except by first hearing them taught. What are the four? First, the establishment of dharma. Second, the establishment of truth. Third, the establishment of principle. Fourth, the establishment of vehicle.
Second, distinguishing this from a related perfection. Now, within this, that which takes ultimate truth as its object, turning without any discrimination, wondrous and pure, should be understood as named the perfection of wisdom. That which takes conventional truth as its object, turning with discrimination, wondrous and pure, should be understood as named the perfection of knowledge. This, one should understand, names their twofold distinction.

items.title: Section: A Second Interpretation of the Final Four Perfections — Five Immeasurables, Ever-Higher Wisdom, Imperviousness to Demons, and Both Kinds of Truth

items.zh: 復有異門。謂無量智，當知說名方便善巧波羅蜜多。悕求後後智殊勝性，當知名願波羅蜜多。一切魔怨不壞道性，當知名力波羅蜜多。如實覺了所知境性，當知名智波羅蜜多。
items.en:
Second, a second meaning; first, skilful means. There is furthermore a different approach: immeasurable wisdom should be understood as named the perfection of skilful means.
Commentary: Regarding "immeasurable wisdom" — this refers to five kinds of immeasurability, one should understand, since bodhisattvas are able to give rise to every skilful function regarding these five immeasurables.
Second, vow. Longing for wisdom ever more excellent still, life after life, should be understood as named the perfection of vow.
Third, power. Imperviousness of the very nature of the path to every demonic, hostile force should be understood as named the perfection of power.
Fourth, knowledge. Genuinely, correctly awakening to the nature of whatever is known should be understood as named the perfection of knowledge.

items.title: Section: Three Brief Conduct-Kinds — the Factors of Awakening, the Six Spiritual Powers, and Maturing Sentient Beings — Closing All Four Kinds Together

items.zh: 四念住等所有一切三十七種菩提分法、四種尋思、四如實智，皆如前說，總名菩薩菩提分法行。如前所說威力品中，菩薩所有六種神通，是名神通行。如前所說二種無量。一、所調伏界無量，二、調伏方便界無量。及成熟品中所說一切成熟有情，總名菩薩成熟有情行。如是四種菩薩妙行，當知普攝一切菩薩所行善行。
items.en:
Second, the conduct of the factors of awakening. The four foundations of mindfulness and all the rest, comprising the thirty-seven factors of awakening, together with the four investigations and four kinds of genuine knowledge, exactly as already explained — all this together is called the bodhisattva's own conduct of the factors of awakening.
Third, the conduct of spiritual powers. The six spiritual powers already explained in the chapter on majestic power are called the conduct of spiritual powers.
Fourth, the conduct of maturing sentient beings. The two immeasurables already explained — the immeasurable realm of those to be tamed, and the immeasurable realm of skilful means for taming them — together with everything explained in the chapter on maturation, are together called the bodhisattva's own conduct of maturing sentient beings.
Second, the conclusion. These four kinds of excellent bodhisattva conduct should be understood to comprehensively gather in every wholesome practice a bodhisattva undertakes.

items.title: Section: Why "Perfection" — Three Aeons of Cultivation, an Utterly Pure Nature, and a Fruit Surpassing Every Lesser Vehicle

items.zh: 應知此中，施等十法，經三大劫阿僧企耶，長時修習乃圓證故；自性清淨體殊勝故；過餘一切世間聲聞、獨覺善根，攝受最勝菩提果故。如是十法最極長時乃能圓證，自性最極清淨殊勝，能得最極菩提妙果，是故說名波羅蜜多。
items.en:
Second, a fuller elaboration on generosity and the rest; first, explaining the meaning of the term "perfection." One should understand that these ten dharmas, generosity and the rest, are cultivated across three great incalculable aeons before genuine, complete realisation is reached; their own intrinsic nature is itself utterly pure and excellent.
Commentary: Regarding "their own intrinsic nature is itself utterly pure and excellent" — the treatise already explained that a bodhisattva, having in sequence perfected the six perfections, is thereby able to realise unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening; each perfection's own nature was explained individually there. One should understand its own substance to be pure and excellent accordingly.
They surpass every wholesome root of every hearer and solitary-realiser in the world, gathering in the most excellent fruit of awakening. Because these ten dharmas require the very longest span of time before genuine, complete realisation, because their own nature is utterly, excellently pure, and because they attain the most excellent, wondrous fruit of awakening, this is why they are named perfections.

items.title: Section: Three Causes for the Sequence — Remedy, Arising, and Ripening-Fruit; and How Each of Six Remedies Its Own Obstacle

items.zh: 應知如是波羅蜜多，由三因緣次第建立。何等為三？一、由對治故；二、由生起故；三、由異熟果故。云何如是波羅蜜多，由對治故，次第建立？謂慳、惡行、於諸有情怨恨逼惱、懈怠、散亂、闇鈍愚癡，如是六法能障菩提；施等六法能為對治，如其所應，建立六種波羅蜜多。當知所餘波羅蜜多即此所攝。如是名為由對治故，次第建立。
items.en:
Second, displaying the meaning of their establishment; first, clarifying the causes; first, naming them. One should understand that these perfections are established in sequence through three causes.
Second, posing the question. What are the three?
Third, listing them. First, through remedy. Second, through arising. Third, through ripening-fruit.
Fourth, explaining; first, through remedy; first, posing the question. Why, through remedy, are they established in this sequence?
Second, explaining; first, presenting the first six. Stinginess, wrongful conduct, resentment and harm towards sentient beings, laziness, distraction, and dull, foolish delusion — these six dharmas are able to obstruct awakening. Generosity and the remaining five dharmas are able to serve as their remedy; exactly as corresponding, the six perfections are established.
Second, subsuming the rest. One should understand that the remaining perfections are themselves subsumed within these.
Third, the conclusion. This is what is meant by establishment through remedy.

blocks.text: The chapter on conduct names four kinds of bodhisattva conduct and adds four perfections to the familiar six, making ten.

"The first three display purified aspiration; the other seven purified conduct." Venerable Miào Jìng: with faith, compassion, and kindness the mind is pure, and the actions flowing from them are pure.

Venerable Miào Jìng: if you can know you are wrong, that is already good, and not easy. Master Cháng Bǎi: even bodhisattvas at the end of the tenth ground bow to the Buddha daily, never forgetting their great benefactor.

The perfections, the factors of awakening, the spiritual powers, and maturing beings. Master Cháng Bǎi: this is the outline of the bodhisattva path. Venerable Miào Jìng: this chapter mainly concerns the stage of resolute practice, where all ten are first trained.
Skilful means, vow, power, and wisdom are added. Master Cháng Bǎi: the seventh ground especially accomplishes skilful means, the ninth power, the tenth wisdom.
Venerable Miào Jìng: a small gift to a dog is nothing special, but dedicating it to supreme awakening is powerful (Day 397).
Master Cháng Bǎi: Amitābha made forty-eight vows, Bhaiṣajyaguru twelve, Samantabhadra ten; every correct vow comes down to seeking awakening above and transforming beings below.
Master Cháng Bǎi: good causes bring happy results and evil causes painful ones: that is the "possible".
Venerable Miào Jìng: both are wisdom, one fundamental, one subsequent. Master Cháng Bǎi: the first is free of names; the second uses names without clinging to them.
"The nature of the path, indestructible by any demon or enemy, is the perfection of power." Master Cháng Bǎi: outer demons are drawn forth by inner ones.
"Completed only over the longest time, utterly pure by nature, attaining the supreme fruit." Master Cháng Bǎi: they carry one from the shore of saṃsāra to the shore of nirvāṇa.
Through remedy, through arising, and through ripening-fruit. Master Cháng Bǎi: the six are set up as remedies for beings' afflictions.
"Outer demons are drawn forth by inner ones." A useful thought when something outside seems to block your practice.

quiz.q: What two meanings do the ten dharmas display, and how are they assigned?
options: the first three show pure aspiration, the other seven pure conduct
quiz.why: "The first three display purified aspiration; the other seven purified conduct." Venerable Miào Jìng: with faith, compassion, and kindness the mind is pure, and the actions flowing from them are pure.

quiz.q: In the sequence, "when one's own affliction suddenly arises, deep shame arises." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: if you can see you're wrong, that's already good — not easy
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: if you can know you're wrong, that's already good — not easy. Master Cháng Bǎi: even while benefiting beings, afflictions sometimes suddenly arise.

quiz.q: Why is offering to the Tathāgata last? What do the lectures say?
options: having accomplished practice one offers right conduct and wealth-and-respect — Miào Jìng: flowers and bowing are wealth-and-respect; Cháng Bǎi: even tenth-ground bodhisattvas bow daily, never forgetting the Buddha's kindness
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: offerings of incense, flowers, and bowing are wealth-and-respect offerings. Master Cháng Bǎi: even bodhisattvas at the end of the tenth ground bow to the Buddha daily, never forgetting their great benefactor.

quiz.q: What four kinds of conduct does the chapter on conduct name?
options: the perfections, factors of awakening, spiritual powers, maturing beings
quiz.why: Conduct of the perfections, of the factors of awakening, of spiritual powers, and of maturing beings. Master Cháng Bǎi: this is the outline of the bodhisattva path; the factors stress calm and insight, the perfections are broader.

quiz.q: According to Venerable Miào Jìng, whom do the ten dharmas of this chapter mainly address?
options: mainly the stage of resolute practice — where these ten should first be trained
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the chapter mainly speaks of the stage of resolute practice, where these ten should first be trained. Master Cháng Bǎi: the level rises ground by ground.

quiz.q: Beyond the six, which four complete the ten perfections?
quiz.why: Skilful means, vow, power, and wisdom. Master Cháng Bǎi: the seventh ground especially accomplishes skilful means, the ninth power, the tenth wisdom.

quiz.q: On the perfection of vow, which specific vows does Master Cháng Bǎi cite, and what principle unites them?
options: Amitābha's forty-eight, Bhaiṣajyaguru's twelve, Samantabhadra's ten — all seeking awakening above and transforming beings below
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: Amitābha made forty-eight vows, Bhaiṣajyaguru twelve, Samantabhadra ten; a bodhisattva's correct vows never depart from seeking awakening above and transforming beings below.

quiz.q: "Purified effort regarding the ten powers." How does Master Cháng Bǎi define "possible" and "impossible"?
options: good cause happy result, evil cause painful result is "possible"; the reverse "impossible"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the principle that good causes bring happy results and evil causes painful ones is "possible"; its reverse "impossible." Venerable Miào Jìng: lawful cause and effect.

quiz.q: The treatise distinguishes 慧 and 智 perfections; the English calls both wisdom. How do the lectures distinguish?
options: both: 慧 is fundamental non-discriminating wisdom; 智 subsequent wisdom, knowing names as provisional without grasping
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: both are wisdom, one fundamental, one subsequent. Master Cháng Bǎi: the former is fundamental non-discriminating wisdom, free of names; the latter uses names without clinging to them.

quiz.q: In the second interpretation, what is the perfection of power?
options: the nature of the path that no demon or enemy can destroy
quiz.why: "The nature of the path, indestructible by any demon or enemy, is the perfection of power." Master Cháng Bǎi: outer demons are drawn forth by inner ones; all arise from one's own mind.

quiz.q: What three reasons does the treatise give for the name "perfection"?
options: longest to complete, utterly pure by nature, yielding the supreme fruit of awakening
quiz.why: "Completed only over the longest time, utterly pure by nature, attaining the supreme fruit — hence perfections." Master Cháng Bǎi: they carry one from saṃsāra's shore to nirvāṇa's.

quiz.q: By which three causes are the perfections established in sequence?
quiz.why: Through remedy, through arising, through ripening-fruit. Master Cháng Bǎi: the six are set up as remedies for beings' afflictions.
